I am thinking about this year's cotton on my 16.1 mu. My husband and I manage it with help from family — six mouths to feed, so I cannot afford a bad harvest. Last year my cotton did okay, so I will mostly do what I did before, with small changes.

For seed, I buy improved Bt cotton seed from the dealer in town. Everyone around me plants Bt cotton — it saves on spraying for bollworm. I will not go back to old seed.

For fertilizer, I use diammonium phosphate as base fertilizer before planting — about 25 kg per mu. Then I topdress with urea when the cotton starts squaring, maybe 20 kg per mu, and again a bit at flowering, another 15 kg urea. I also put some potassium, one bag of potassium sulfate split across a few mu — about 10 kg per mu. My neighbor got better bolls when he added potassium, so I keep doing it. In total that gives me around 20 kg nitrogen per mu, 12 kg phosphorus, 10 kg potassium. I would rather put a little extra than see thin plants.

Water — I have a well, so I irrigate 4 times: once after planting if the soil is dry, once at squaring, once at flowering-boll, once at boll filling. Cotton here needs water at flowering or the bolls drop.

Pesticide — even with Bt seed I still spray. Aphids come early, then spider mites in hot weather, then maybe late bollworm and for defoliation before picking. I spray about 6 times total. Skipping sprays is how you lose a crop.

Tillage — I plough after last year's stalks, then rotary before planting. I use plough because the soil gets hard.

Yield — last year I got around 270 kg seed cotton per mu. I hope for 280 this year.
